title: Mauretania
capsule: Mauretania was an ancient Berber kingdom occupying the northwestern corner of Africa, roughly corresponding to northern Morocco and the western Algerian coast, inhabited by the Mauri and ruled by indigenous Berber kings from at least the third century BCE. Bocchus I, king in the late second century BCE, betrayed his son-in-law Jugurtha to Rome in 105 BCE, securing Roman alliance; the kingdom became a formal Roman client state under Juba II (r. 25 BCE – 23 CE), an erudite Romanized Berber prince installed by Augustus who made Caesarea (modern Cherchell) his capital. After Ptolemy of Mauretania was executed by Caligula in 40 CE, Emperor Claudius annexed the territory in 44 CE, reorganizing it into the provinces of Mauretania Caesariensis and Mauretania Tingitana.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The general extent of Mauretania is well documented in Roman geographical and historical sources, but the inland boundary with Numidia and the southern desert fringe is approximate rather than precisely mapped.
